transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-10-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Lina Brooks (Redwood Product), Dana Patel (CTO - Kepler Health), Tariq Ahmed (Eng Manager), Sofia Li (Infra), Ben Ortiz (FinOps)

00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros?
00:06 Dana Patel: Hi, Dana here, CTO at Kepler. we've got Tariq and Sofia from infra and Ben from finance.
00:12 Tariq Ahmed: Tariq, eng manager, mainly to scope integration and latency goals.
00:16 Ben Ortiz: Ben, FinOps, mostly cost questions.
:21 Avery Chen: perfect, we'll do a 35-40 minute console walkthrough and leave time for security and pilot questions. Marcus will show the per-route panels.
01:02 Marcus Rivera: ok jumping in - this is the Console -> Usage page. top left you'll see total tokens, active routes, and lat p50/p95. note: sometimes the auto-transcript shows product names weird, we call this the usage atlas internally.
02:10 Marcus Rivera: route list on the left is pulled from your routing keys; we group by route id then by model family. here we can click into a single route - e.g., patient-summarize-prod.
03:02 Marcus Rivera: the per-route view shows throughput (req/s), tokens per request, 95th latency, and cost per request. cost here is computed from model token rates plus infra amortization.
03:44 Sofia Li: question — how are you attributing infra cost? is it by GPU-hours or by tokens?
03:49 Marcus Rivera: good question — by default console uses token-weighted infra attribution: GPU-hours are mapped to model variants and then to routes by token-usage per window. you can toggle to per-instance hour if you prefer exact cluster chargeback.
04:20 Ben Ortiz: does that mean small chat routes get overcharged if they cause many short requests?
04:25 Marcus Rivera: can happen; we have a cap and smoothing window. also Optimize can suggest batching or caching policies for those routes to reduce per-request overhead.
05:00 Marcus Rivera: note on sampling: for high-traffic routes we sample 10% by default for detailed traces to avoid egress costs; you can change sample rate per route.
05:43 Dana Patel: what's the retention on request-level traces? HIPAA-ish people ask.
05:48 Marcus Rivera: default is 30 days for traces, 13 months for aggregated metrics. for private/dedicated you can opt for longer retention and self-hosted logs. all PII redaction options are available.
06:20 Avery Chen: quick pause — security summary: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and KMS integrations for key control. Marcus will share the security FAQ after the call.
07:05 Marcus Rivera: back to the demo — cost breakdown panel here splits model unit costs and infra amortization. you can toggle quantization profiles and see instant delta. e.g., switching to 4-bit quant reduces model unit cost by ~30% on this workload.
07:55 Tariq Ahmed: for our regulated runs we need KMS HSM and no shared model cache; how does private work?
08:02 Marcus Rivera: Private deployment gives you customer-managed control plane and option to disable prefix caching and run with customer KMS; on-prem package supports air-gapped config. one caveat: you lose some cross-customer economies of scale so infra unit cost rises.
09:15 Dana Patel: latency SLOs — we need p95 < 300ms for the summarization route. possible?
09:22 Marcus Rivera: yes on Dedicated with optimized kernels and continuous batching you can hit that for 1-2k rpm. dependent on sequence length distribution. we'll run a short benchmark with your sample to size correctly.
10:02 Marcus Rivera: showing the cost attribution timeline — you can select custom windows, group by model version, route, or user team. many customers use routes->team mapping for chargeback.
10:40 Ben Ortiz: do you expose per-token prices per model in CSV? we need to map to our internal billing.
10:45 Marcus Rivera: yes, export CSV button includes token units, infra allocation, and effective per-token price per route. I'll attach a sample.
11:20 Marcus Rivera: toggling to the anomalies view — console flags sudden cost spikes and surface correlated changes like shifts in token distribution or new model rollouts.
12:05 Dana Patel: how do rollouts work if a canary causes cost regression?
12:12 Marcus Rivera: we integrate rollout policies; you can set cost regression thresholds. if a canary increases cost per request by > X% we auto-roll back to the previous model and open a trace.
13:05 Avery Chen: underpinning tech note — we maintain a KV cache for prefix reuse; this reduces tokens and latency for multi-turn chat. it's configurable per route.
14:00 Tariq Ahmed: any recommended Optimize settings for multi-turn clinician chat?
14:08 Marcus Rivera: for multi-turn set KV cache TTL longer, enable prefix caching and use adaptive batching with max latency 150ms. Optimize can simulate the token savings for a sample trace.
15:10 Marcus Rivera: demo: here's a 'what-if' toggler — choose quantization + batching profile and it projects cost delta and latency impact over 7 days.
16:02 Ben Ortiz: show me an example where we cut cost 40% without hurting p95 too much.
16:07 Marcus Rivera: sure — on an example route we moved from fp16 hosted to ded 4-bit with a slightly higher p50 but same p95 due to kernel ops. cost down ~38%.
17:05 Dana Patel: curious — if we go Dedicated and then scale back, how do commitments work?
17:12 Avery Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity; we offer monthly committed tiers with burst-to-hosted for spikes. contracts can be monthly or annual. Marcus will send a sample commitment table.
18:02 Marcus Rivera: switching to dashboards — you can create a route dashboard and pin cost, latency, failure rate panels. these dashboards can be shared with stakeholders with RBAC.
18:48 Sofia Li: RBAC depth — can we restrict access to only cost metrics for Finance?
18:52 Marcus Rivera: yes, RBAC can restrict to routes and metric categories. SAML groups map to roles.
19:30 Marcus Rivera: now jumping to debugging traces — for a single request you can see token timeline, KV hits, batch grouping, and exact model variant used. note: transcript sometimes labels this 'K V cache' or 'K-V cache' in exports.
20:15 Tariq Ahmed: for throughput planning, what's the continuous batching overhead?
20:20 Marcus Rivera: continuous batching introduces a micro-queue, latency depends on the batching window and target. usually <10ms for high throughput, but spikes can add 10-50ms if traffic bursts are uneven.
21:05 Ben Ortiz: the cost model — can we bring our own price per GPU-hour to reflect our internal pricing?
21:12 Marcus Rivera: yes, you can override infra unit costs in the account settings to match internal chargeback. console will recalc effective per-token prices.
22:00 Marcus Rivera: now an example of per-route anomaly: notice on the left patient-summarize-prod had a sudden token jump at 09:12 UTC. drill in — it was due to model_version:v2 with longer outputs. you can set alert to notify Slack.
23:10 Dana Patel: perfect — our primary worry is silent regressions when LLM rollouts change output verbosity and blow up costs.
23:18 Marcus Rivera: that's why we tie evals to prompt sets and run smoke tests during rollouts; regressions trigger a rollback. console also shows expected token delta for a model change.
24:00 Marcus Rivera: questions about integrations? we have CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or you can send raw JSON to your logging sink.
24:40 Sofia Li: for our VPC requirements — do you support AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering?
24:45 Marcus Rivera: both. Private offers customer-managed control plane, VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your network policy.
25:10 Dana Patel: what about audit logs access for compliance?
25:15 Marcus Rivera: audit logs are available for all admin events, with export to S3 and optional SIEM hooks. we can include API call logs and model-rollout events.
26:00 Avery Chen: ok let's shift to pilot discussion — we propose a 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding, week 1 smoke tests + bench, week 2 pilot traffic, week 3 sizing and recommendations.
26:25 Ben Ortiz: what would you need from our side to start?
26:30 Avery Chen: a week of representative traffic in CSV/ndjson, SLOs, and security contact. also a service account for API keys and possibly a small dedicated pool for the test.
26:55 Sofia Li: we need an NDA addendum for HIPAA data flows; is Redwoods privacy attestation available?
27:02 Avery Chen: yes, we have a HIPAA addendum and can provide BAAs for Private deployments. I'll attach the legal pack.
28:00 Marcus Rivera: back to the console, showing Optimize suggestions panel — it lists routes with highest potential savings, estimated impact and suggested config (batch window, quantization, cache TTL). you can apply suggestions in one click to a staging route.
29:10 Tariq Ahmed: do those suggestions get validated automatically?
29:15 Marcus Rivera: suggestions are simulation-based using historical traces; you must run them on staging or allow a dry-run which will simulate at runtime without impacting production.
30:05 Marcus Rivera: here's the billing export — shows raw token units, model unit costs, infra allocation, and per-route effective cost. useful for your internal invoices.
30:50 Ben Ortiz: will the export match invoices or be an approximation?
30:55 Marcus Rivera: the console export is the source for invoices on hosted accounts. for Dedicated we reconcile against committed usage and show adjustments.
31:30 Dana Patel: any notable gotchas for us migrating from self-hosted runtime?
31:36 Marcus Rivera: you might need to convert your model variants to Redwood-compatible formats and re-validate tokenization differences. we have tooling to help. also pay attention to KV cache semantics which may differ.
32:20 Avery Chen: security quick-check: we'll send SAML metadata template and KMS provider list.
32:30 Sofia Li: good. also want to validate key rotation windows.
32:34 Marcus Rivera: rotation supported, and we can automate key rollover with your KMS if you provide perms.
33:05 Marcus Rivera: demo wrap: recorded alert for cost spike, create a dashboard, export CSV, apply Optimize suggestion in staging, and project cost delta.
34:00 Dana Patel: that's useful. Ben — do you have any finance-specific questions?
34:04 Ben Ortiz: yes — can we get a 90-day forecast given current growth assumptions?
34:08 Marcus Rivera: yes, we can run a forecast model if you provide growth rates and retention. I'll include a sample forecast file.
35:00 Avery Chen: open Q&A — anyone want to drill into per-route access patterns?
35:12 Tariq Ahmed: can we get raw request/response latencies exported for our SREs?
35:17 Marcus Rivera: yes, request-level logs can be exported; for high-volume routes enable sampling to keep size manageable.
36:00 Dana Patel: last question, who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
36:05 Avery Chen: I'll own the commercial part and Marcus will own the technical onboarding. Lina will be PM contact.
36:20 Marcus Rivera: noted.
36:30 Avery Chen: recap and next steps: we'll send Dedicated pricing and pilot contract, sample CSV export and security docs. pilot kickoff call scheduled, tentative 2026-10-26.
37:10 Dana Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
37:20 Tariq Ahmed: thanks.
37:25 Ben Ortiz: thanks all.
37:30 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mislabels and homophone substitutions (Redwood/Dedicate vs Dedicated), proper nouns sometimes garbled.
